_comment: Collection roster. Ported from haven-web/src/lib/chains.ts GATES — same contracts, same
thresholds, same editorial premises, trimmed to one sentence for a phone.
Bundled rather than fetched because there is no public Arkiv network to discover communities
from yet (see the index status note in haven-web/src/lib/chains.ts). When one exists this file
becomes the offline fallback and the live roster comes from the index.
Deliberately absent: prices. The web page reads live floor prices from market data; a price
frozen into an APK would be wrong within a day, and a wrong price is a trust problem. The
'get access' link opens the marketplace, where the real number is.
The 'gate' block is read by internal code only and is never shown to a reader.

collections.name: Forgotten Runes Wizard's Cult
collections.premise: A cult that produces its own animation and serialised film. Masters, stems and unreleased cuts are exactly the material that should never sit on a platform.

collections.name: Chain Runners
collections.premise: On-chain characters with a written world around them. The canon is community-authored, which makes where it lives a governance question.

collections.name: mfers
collections.premise: A CC0 culture that generates more derivative work than any single site could host. An archive its holders control is the only stable copy.

collections.name: Opepen Edition
collections.premise: A long-running set release with process, revisions and correspondence behind it — the parts of an artwork that usually vanish.

collections.name: Autoglyphs
collections.premise: 512 pieces of primary art-historical material. Provenance, scholarship and interviews belong with the holders, not with a gallery site.

collections.name: Blitmap
collections.premise: Community-composed art with a documented authorship chain. The source files matter as much as the outputs.

collections.name: Terraforms
collections.premise: Fully on-chain terrain with a deep technical record behind it. The writing about the work is as scarce as the work.

collections.name: SuperRare
collections.premise: A curation DAO sitting on two decades of artist material at full resolution — the masters, not the transcodes.

collections.name: Friends With Benefits
collections.premise: A membership that has always been token-gated. Talks, sets and dinners recorded for members are the canonical case for an archive.

collections.name: WHALE
collections.premise: A social token backed by a real collection. The vault has a story, and the story is worth more to members than to the public.

collections.name: Rally
collections.premise: Creator economies whose back catalogues outlived the platforms that hosted them. That is the failure this protocol exists to answer.

collections.name: Audius
collections.premise: Music, and the unreleased half of every catalogue. Stems and sessions are precisely what an artist will not upload anywhere.

collections.name: Nouns
collections.premise: One vote, one holder, and a treasury that has funded hundreds of things. The evidence of what it funded is a public good with a private half.

collections.name: Juicebox
collections.premise: The funding rail for hundreds of small treasuries. Every campaign leaves records its contributors have a claim on.

collections.name: Kleros
collections.premise: Dispute resolution runs on evidence. Evidence needs to be encrypted, addressable, and readable only by the panel.

collections.name: Radicle
collections.premise: Sovereign code collaboration — a project already committed to the premise that infrastructure should not be able to remove your work.
